0.headline: AceVector IPO subscribed 64% so far on Day 2; retail portion fully booked
0.heading: AceVector IPO subscribed 64% so far on Day 2; retail portion fully booked
0.intro: The initial public offering of AceVector continued to see a measured response on the second day of bidding, with the issue subscribed 64 percent as of 1:45 pm on September 28, according to NSE data.
0.body:
The initial public offering of AceVector continued to see a measured response on the second day of bidding, with the issue subscribed 64 percent as of 1:45 pm on September 28, according to NSE data.

The Rs 420-crore IPO received bids for 4,78,72,656 equity shares against 7,42,29,166 shares on offer. Retail investors led the demand, with the portion reserved for them subscribed 1.07 times. The non-institutional investor (NII) category was subscribed 75 percent.

In the grey market, AceVector shares were commanding a premium of 3.12 percent on the morning of September 28, according to InvestorGain. Based on the upper end of the IPO price band of Rs 32, the grey market premium indicates an implied price of around Rs 33 per share.

Read Also: Runwal Enterprises IPO subscribed 50% on Day 2 so far; check latest GMP

However, the grey market premium (GMP) is an unofficial indicator of market sentiment and can change before listing. It does not guarantee the actual listing price of the shares.

Ahead of the public issue, AceVector raised Rs 189 crore from 14 anchor investors through the allotment of 5.9 crore shares. The shares were allotted at Rs 32 apiece, the upper end of the IPO price band.

Negen Undiscovered Value Fund emerged as the largest investor in the anchor book, acquiring 1.24 crore equity shares for around Rs 40 crore.

Singularity AMC, which is mentored by investor Madhusudan Kela, picked up 84.37 lakh shares for nearly Rs 27 crore. Meanwhile, 360 ONE Asset Management’s Turnaround Opportunities Fund acquired 62.49 lakh shares for around Rs 20 crore.

Check IPO News Here

The Kunal Bahl, Rohit Kumar Bansal and SoftBank-promoted company opened its Rs 420-crore IPO for subscription on September 25. The issue will close on September 29, with the price band fixed at Rs 30-32 per share.

The IPO comprises a fresh issue of equity shares worth Rs 287 crore, while existing shareholders, including promoter Starfish, are offering 4.15 crore shares for sale through the offer-for-sale (OFS) route.

AceVector operates the e-commerce marketplace Snapdeal and is backed by investors including SoftBank, Nexus Venture Partners, FIH Business Global and eBay International AG.

The company plans to use Rs 132 crore from the net proceeds of the fresh issue towards marketing and business promotion expenses for its marketplace business.

IIFL Capital Services, CLSA India and Systematix Corporate Services are the merchant bankers to the issue.

1.headline: Shah Investor's IPO subscribed 7% on Day 1 so far; check GMP
1.heading: Shah Investor's IPO subscribed 7% on Day 1 so far; check GMP
1.intro: Shah Investor's IPO allotment is likely to be finalised by October 1, while the equity shares are expected to start trading on the bourses on October 6.
1.body:
The Rs 90.17-crore initial public offering (IPO) of Shah Investor's Home was subscribed 7 percent on the first day of bidding so far, with the issue receiving demand for over 2.75 lakh shares against 37.79 lakh shares on offer till 1:10 pm on Monday.

The portion reserved for Retail Individual Investors (RIIs) was subscribed 11 percent, while the quota for Non-Institutional Investors (NIIs) was booked 7 percent so far.

Ahmedabad-based Shah Investor's Home, a retail stock broking company, opened its IPO for subscription on September 28.
Check All IPO News
Shah Investor's IPO GMP Today Price
According to platforms tracking grey market activities, the shares of Shah Investor's IPO are commanding a GMP of up to 7 percent. Investorgain quoted a GMP of Rs 12 for the shares of the company, indicating a listing gain of 7.19 percent. Meanwhile, IPO Watch, quoted a GMP of 5.99 percent.

The company aims to raise Rs 90.16 crore through the IPO and is seeking a valuation of Rs 353.25 crore at the upper end of the price band of Rs 159-167 per share.

Shah Investor's Home competes with smallcap listed peers such as SMC Global Securities, Share India Securities and Arihant Capital Markets.

The company intends to use Rs 60 crore of the net IPO proceeds for working capital requirements, with the remaining funds earmarked for general corporate purposes.

On the financial front, the company reported a profit of Rs 13.2 crore for the year ended March 2026, down 43.5 per cent from Rs 23.4 crore in the previous year. Revenue during the same period declined 24.2 per cent to Rs 71.5 crore from Rs 94.3 crore.

The IPO share allotment is likely to be finalised by October 1, while the equity shares are expected to start trading on the bourses on October 6.

2.headline: Defence electronics maker Tonbo Imaging gets SEBI approval for IPO
2.heading: Defence electronics maker Tonbo Imaging gets SEBI approval for IPO
2.intro: Defence electronics maker Tonbo Imaging has received SEBI approval for its proposed IPO, with existing shareholders set to sell up to 1.81 crore equity shares through an offer for sale
2.body:
Tonbo Imaging India, a defence electronics manufacturer, has received approval from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) to launch its initial public offering (IPO), in a move that will allow existing shareholders to sell up to 18.09 million equity shares. The proposed issue will be entirely an offer for sale (OFS), meaning the company itself will not receive proceeds from the shares being sold.

The OFS will include shares held by promoter selling shareholders, a promoter group selling shareholder and investor selling shareholders. JM Financial and IIFL Capital Services are the book running lead managers for the issue.

Tonbo among key thermal imaging suppliers

Founded in 2003, Tonbo Imaging became a defence-focused product manufacturer in 2012 after its promoters acquired its erstwhile parent. The company is promoted by Arvind Kondangi Lakshmikum­ar, Ankit Kumar and Cecilia D’Souza, who have worked together for more than two decades across defence programmes, product engineering, research and development, fundraising and international business.

According to the Frost &amp; Sullivan report cited in the company's draft red herring prospectus (DRHP), Tonbo was the largest manufacturer by sales value of thermal imaging systems supplied to government and defence agencies in India between FY24 and FY26.

The company also accounted for 94.3 percent of India's thermal imaging exports by units during the same period, according to the report.

Tonbo had more than 28,000 systems deployed across 24 countries as of March 31, 2026. Its product portfolio includes thermal imaging cores, weapon sights, thermal binoculars, targeting systems, missile seekers, fire-control systems and missile-guidance systems.

The company has also built its own intellectual property portfolio. It has owned 100 percent of its intellectual property since FY24, covering areas such as optics, embedded software and electronics. Its manufacturing partners include Kaynes Technology India and Avalon Technology.

The company counts Qualcomm Ventures, Artiman, Celesta, Edelweiss Value and Growth Fund, HBL Engineering, Tenacity Ventures, Export-Import Bank of India and Florintree among its investors. The IPO will therefore provide an exit opportunity to some of the company's existing shareholders through the OFS.
